text: What is a minimal reproduction, and why is producing one usually most of the fix?
choices: The original program with the inputs reduced, so the failing data is small.
A test case that runs in under a second, so the debugging loop stays fast.
A version of the program with logging added at every level of the call stack.
The smallest program that still shows the bug; producing it forces you to remove everything irrelevant, which is exactly the process of localising the cause.
explanation: Reduction is diagnosis. Every piece you delete without the bug disappearing is a piece proven innocent, and by the time twelve lines remain there is nowhere left for the fault to hide. It also happens to be what a maintainer needs in order to help you, which is why Chapter 35's exercise on contributing to a project asks specifically for one.
